user-code-on-own-domain-01.graded_text: The target layout serves people's HTML and JavaScript from a separate registrable domain, not from any subdomain of plinth.example.

votes.e: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md Phase 2: "Register one separate registrable domain for user content." and "| `<name>.<content-domain>` | The person's files, same-origin again, sandbox header removed. `localStorage` works. |"; also "The usual fix is to serve user code from a **separate registrable domain** and have the product's address frame it."

user-code-on-own-domain-02.graded_text: The reason given is that every subdomain of one registrable domain is the same site: script on a sibling subdomain can set cookies for the parent domain and ride same-site requests, which lets it interfere with sign-in (login CSRF or session confusion) or reach session tokens.

votes.e: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md: "For the browser, every `*.plinth.example` host is the **same site** as `app.plinth.example`"; "Script on any app host can set a cookie for `Domain=plinth.example`, so it can sign a visitor into an attacker's account on `app.plinth.example`"; "Requests from an app to `app.plinth.example` count as same-site, so `SameSite=Lax` gives no CSRF protection"; "Any app can read the visitor's session from `document.cookie`".

user-code-on-own-domain-03.graded_text: The short <name>.plinth.example address is kept as Plinth's own page, which frames the app served from the other domain, so visitors still see the Plinth address.

votes.e: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md Phase 2: "| `<name>.plinth.example` | **Product-owned** frame page. The short address stays what people see and share. |" and "`<name>.plinth.example/<path>?<query>` returns a small product page. Its iframe `src` is `https://<name>.<content-domain>/<path>?<query>`".

user-code-on-own-domain-04.graded_text: Each app gets its own origin on the content domain, such as a label per app, so one app cannot read another's storage.

votes.e: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md Phase 2 serves each app at its own label "`<name>.<content-domain>` | The person's files, same-origin again", with rationale "Every app has its own origin, so `localStorage` is already per app" and resolver "CONTENT_HOST_SUFFIX <content-domain> -> resolveUserContentOrigin(name)".

user-code-on-own-domain-05.graded_text: Until the separate domain can be set up after the freeze, people's code runs with an opaque origin, through a sandbox (for example a CSP sandbox header) without allow-same-origin, and the plan says this costs the apps their browser storage. It does not keep serving people's code as the top-level document on plinth.example subdomains during the beta.

votes.e: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md "## Phase 1: beta, during the freeze (ship this)": "Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms allow-modals allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox allow-downloads"; "The `sandbox` directive leaves out `allow-same-origin`, so the app's document runs in an **opaque origin**"; "**Cost: apps lose browser storage during the beta.** An opaque origin has no `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, cookies, or service workers." D1: "Recommended: ship Phase 1 as written" and "Not on the list: shipping as it is today."

blocking: [opus-for-opus] Phase 1 private-app CORS lets any sandboxed page read private apps: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md "the edge answers with the exact `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null` plus `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` only when a valid access cookie is present", with the cookie "`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None; Path=/`". Every Plinth app (and any sandboxed iframe anywhere) has `Origin: null`, so a hostile public app can `fetch('https://<private>.plinth.example/...', {credentials:'include'})` for a viewer holding the grant; the SameSite=None cookie is attached and ACAO `null` lets the attacker read invited-only content. (withdrawn)

[opus-for-opus] The same `SameSite=None` access cookie (D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md "`__Host-plinth_app_access` ... `SameSite=None`") is sent on cross-site subresource loads from any site, so a private app's scripts/JSON can be included cross-site (XSSI) by any page an invited viewer visits; no `Sec-Fetch-Site`/`Origin` check at the edge is specified. (withdrawn)
